subject: Notable improvement in spatiotemporal random slope model fit: any insights?

messages.author: a96aa45411c16ae6
messages.subject: Notable improvement in spatiotemporal random slope model fit: any insights?
parts:
Dear R-INLA community:

Hello, I have been using R-INLA for a couple of years. For my own project, I employed several random slope models with and without spatiotemporally structured components from a dataset of 3,108 (the number of spatial entities) * 14 (the number of total time points):

form.m40 <- Mortrate ~
  f(GEOID, model = "bym", graph = graph, constr = TRUE) +
  f(year1, model = 'ar1', constr = TRUE) +
  f(GEOID1, UELAG1, model = "bym", graph = graph, constr = TRUE) +
  f(year2, UELAG1, model = 'ar1', constr = TRUE) +
  UELAG1 + PELDER + PNONWHITE + MEDINCOME + PUNIVABOVE + PPOVTBELOW + PRURAL + PRENTER + PHSINGLE
form.m4IV <- update(form.m40, ~ . + f(GEOID2, UELAG1, model = "bym", graph = graph, group = year3, control.group = list(model = "rw1"),
                          constr = TRUE) )

I used INLA version 21.03.20 (with PARDISO solver) to fit the model with form.m4IV, which took around 60 hours to get precise modes (mode.status==0) and wide marginal distributions. Recently I had a chance to rerun the models with the recent testing version of INLA (21.11.01), the model fit was notably improved that it just took six hours to attain preferable mode status (mode.status==0) with more concentrated marginal distributions than the those of previous model fit with the old version of INLA. Although I read through the package news and update records, I am not still very sure what made such an improvement. It can be guessed there was an improvement in the optimization module (e.g. "Smart Gradient" referred in R-INLA Project - News) in the package. Does anyone have insights on the improvement of the model fitting procedure in recent versions of INLA?

Thank you very much.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Notable improvement in spatiotemporal random slope model fit: any insights?
parts:
yes, that is not surprising at all

you can probably get even more speedup updating to the recent version
(require R-4.1), and adding

library(INLA)
inla.setOption(inla.mode="experimental")

please add option

scale.model=TRUE

when using model bym, rw1, rw2 or besag [ (f(..., scale.model=TRUE) ]

Dear Dr. Rue:

I appreciate you and your team to work hard to enhance the package.
Attached are codes and data for reproducibility. You might run the code with minimal edits to specify the path of the RData, the PARDISO license key location, and a thread configuration to use as many threads as you can use in your machine. For your information, after applying scale.model=TRUE, it took 22 hours to get preferable mode status (mode.status==0).

Thank you for your time.

Best,
